name: Jomon Sugi on Yakushima (縄文杉)
why: A long day into the cedar forest of Yakushima: eight kilometres on an old logging railway, then roots and steps up to a cedar thousands of years old.
book: From 1 March to 30 November cars may not drive to the Arakawa trailhead: take the Arakawa hiking bus from the Yakusugi Museum, ticket bought in advance. Put a climbing registration form in the box at the trailhead.
water: Water at the Okabu trail entrance, above Wilson's stump and at Jomon Sugi. Carry 1.5 litres and lunch; there is nothing to buy.
dangers: One of the wettest places in Japan: rain gear always, streams rise fast in heavy rain.
The railway sleepers and bridges are slippery; some bridges have no full handrail.
Trolleys still use the track: step aside at once when one comes.
Toilets are few: carry a portable toilet bag (collection boxes at the trailhead).
turnaround: Not at Jomon Sugi by 12:00: turn back, so that you are on the railway before dark and catch the last bus.

points.name: Arakawa trailhead and the tram line
points.note: About 600 m. The first 8 km follow the forest railway past the old Kosugidani village site: flat but long, single file.

points.name: Okabu trail entrance
points.note: End of the railway, toilets and water. From here the path climbs on roots and wooden steps.

points.name: Wilson's stump (Wilson-kabu)
points.note: A cedar cut about 400 years ago, hollow inside: from one spot the opening makes the shape of a heart.

points.name: Jomon Sugi
points.note: About 1,300 m. The great cedar, seen from a wooden deck. Takatsuka hut is 10 minutes further. Back the same way.
